question: Explain the different types of assessment provided under the CGST Act, 2017.

points.label: Self-assessment
points.description: Every registered person assesses the tax payable by himself and furnishes a return for each tax period.

points.label: Provisional assessment
points.description: Where a taxable person cannot determine the value of goods or services or the rate of tax, he may request the proper officer in writing to allow payment on a provisional basis; the officer passes an order allowing it, the person executes a bond with security, and a final assessment follows within the time allowed.
keywords: unable to determine value or rate

points.label: Scrutiny of returns
points.description: The proper officer may scrutinise a return to verify its correctness and tell the registered person of any discrepancy, seeking an explanation; if the explanation is accepted, no further action is taken, otherwise the officer may start audit, inspection or demand proceedings.

points.label: Assessment of non-filers of returns
points.description: If a registered person fails to file a return even after a notice, the officer may assess the tax to the best of his judgment using the available material; the order is deemed withdrawn if a valid return is filed within the time allowed after service of the order.

points.label: Assessment of unregistered persons
points.description: Where a taxable person liable to register fails to do so, or whose registration has been cancelled but who was liable to pay tax, the officer may assess the tax to the best of his judgment after issuing a show cause notice and giving an opportunity of being heard.

points.label: Summary assessment
points.description: Where the officer has evidence of a tax liability and delay would harm the revenue, he may, with the prior permission of the Additional or Joint Commissioner, assess the liability immediately; the order can be withdrawn on application by the person if found erroneous.
